posts.body_html:
I sorta did a half a$$ job photographing just how amazing the California Carnivores nepenthes collection. The greenhouse is packed to the max with nothing but desirable species and hybrids of Nepenthes, and the longer you stand there, the more you'll end up seeing. If you have the chance to pay a visit, it's something worth seeing. For those of us who can't make it, well at least there's a few photos to enjoy:


Pretty big trap on N. hamata:



another shot of N. hamata, hard to get tired of that amazing peristome:



A big old upper pitcher of N. hamata. Never seen anything like this in person, it was crazy:


Close up:


probably aristolochioides x bongso (for legal purposes, we like to call the latter species "Water-pipeso):







absolutely love this mouse trap lookin hybrid:







River...or rather highland forest Monsta:



Straight up biggie smallz:


upper pitcher of N. alba:





Maybe N. veitchii?




froggie:



Some beautiful color forms of N.ampullaria:

I recognize spectabilis x aristo, veitchii, lowii x truncata, chaniana x veitchii I think....this is definitely an obsession I stand behind
Nepenthes are actually my favorite carnivores; Sarracenia come in a somewhat distant second by comparison.
